title: rift linkage and inheritance determine collisional mountain belt evolution
core_idea: Use coupled 3D upper‑mantle‑scale geodynamic models and a surface processes model to investigate how the geometry, linkage and offset of pre‑collisional rift basins (including stepping, branching and transfer zones) control rift inversion and the 3D evolution of continent–continent collisional mountain belts. The study aims to quantify governing physical principles of 3D inversion tectonics and apply the approach as a diagnostic template for natural examples (Greater Caucasus, Atlas, Pyrenees).
tldr: Investigate, with coupled 3D geodynamic and landscape models, how segmented and offset pre‑collisional rift architectures and their linkage influence rift inversion and the three‑dimensional development of collisional mountain belts; objectives are to extract key characteristics, quantify physical controls, and relate topography to deep lithospheric structure for natural cases.
